entry.title: LinkedIn Strips Formatting — So I Built a Tool to Preserve It
entry.summary:
Have you ever pasted a post into LinkedIn and thought… “Wait… where did all my formatting go?” Your bold disappeared. italics vanished. I hit this problem every single time I copied content from GPT, Notion, or Google Docs. So I dug into why this happens. Here’s the truth 👇 bold, italic, underline, or strikethrough. But you’ve probably noticed something interesting… Some posts do keep their formatting. That’s because they use Unicode characters, not actual formatting. So I built a small tool to fix this 👇 🚀 LinkedIn AI Formatter ✅ You paste content copied from GPT / Notion / Docs ❌ It does NOT add new formatting
Just preservation. Nothing more. Supported formatting: 𝗕𝗼𝗹𝗱 Numbered lists If writing on LinkedIn matters to you — Try it here 👇 https://linkedin-ai-formatter.vercel.app 💻 Open Source at https://github.com/coderomm/linkedin-ai-formatter-app Would genuinely love feedback — especially from people who write regularly on LinkedIn. Building this in public 🚀 More small improvements coming.

entry.title: From Curiosity to Creation: Every Developer’s Real Journey
entry.summary:
🚀 From Curiosity to Creation: Every Developer’s Real Journey
Most people think developers are born with keyboards in their hands.
Truth is — every developer starts with confusion, errors, and curiosity. At first, everything feels overwhelming: What language should I learn? Why is this error not going away? Am I even good enough for this field? If you’re here, reading this — you’re already ahead. You don’t “find” talent.
You build it by: Writing bad code Breaking things Googling the same error 10 times Learning one small concept every day Consistency beats intelligence every single time. Frameworks will change.
Libraries will get deprecated.
AI tools will evolve. But fundamentals remain: Logic Problem solving Clear thinking Clean communication Master the basics. Everything else becomes easier. AI won’t replace developers. use AI wisely will replace those who don’t. Use AI to: Learn faster Debug smarter Explore ideas Not to stop thinking. Don’t wait to be perfect. Share your progress Push imperfect projects Write about what you’re learning Your future opportunities come from visibility + consistency. Every expert you admire was once: Stuck Confused Self-doubting The only difference? Keep building.
Keep learning.
Your code matters. Happy coding 👨‍💻✨

To tap into that niche — and make it practical at scale — the Allen Institute for AI (Ai2) introduced Bolmo, a new family of models that leverage its Olmo 3 models by “bytefiying” them and reusing their backbone and capabilities. The company launched two versions, Bolmo 7B and Bolmo 1B, which are “the first fully open byte-level language model,” according to Ai2. The company said the two models performed competitively with — and in some cases surpassed — other byte-level and character-based models.

entry.title: Why agentic AI needs a new category of customer data
entry.summary:
Presented by Twilio
The customer data infrastructure powering most enterprises was architected for a world that no longer exists: one where marketing interactions could be captured and processed in batches, where campaign timing was measured in days (not milliseconds), and where "personalization" meant inserting a first name into an email template. Conversational AI has shattered those assumptions. AI agents need to know what a customer just said, the tone they used, their emotional state, and their complete history with a brand instantly to provide relevant guidance and effective resolution. This fast-moving stream of conversational signals (tone, urgency, intent, sentiment) represents a fundamentally different category of customer data.
